# Overview

`sam-tagger` is a SAM/BAM tagger and amplicon-sequencing QC statistics generator.
It reads the minimap2 `cs` (alignment comparison) tag and produces, in one pass
per command, either a tagged BAM or Parquet statistics. It is split into **four
focused subcommands**, each with a fixed I/O contract (one well-defined output).

In a typical amplicon pipeline it sits right after alignment (the `cs` tag is
produced by `minimap2 --cs`, or by any cs-tagging step your pipeline uses):

```
minimap2 (--cs)  ──▶  sam-tagger
```

## The four subcommands

| Command       | Positional arguments        | Writes                                              | Read-only? |
|---------------|-----------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|------------|
| `annotate`    | `INPUT-BAM OUTPUT-BAM`      | tagged BAM (or CRAM/SAM), optional FASTQ + Parquet  | no         |
| `error-stats` | `INPUT-BAM CONFIG`          | 7 error Parquet files                               | yes        |
| `pileup`      | `INPUT-BAM OUTPUT`          | 1 pileup Parquet                                    | yes        |
| `qc-summary`  | `INPUT-BAM OUTPUT`          | 1 per-reference QC Parquet                          | yes        |

Every subcommand also accepts `-i/--input-bam` (and `-o/--output` where there is
an output) instead of positionals, `-v` (repeat for INFO/DEBUG/TRACE), and `-h`.

# Installation

`pysam` is provided through **conda-forge / bioconda** (a reliable htslib build),
not PyPI, so install with conda/mamba/pixi rather than pip:

```bash
# conda / mamba
conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda sam-tagger

# pixi (in a project workspace)
pixi add -c conda-forge -c bioconda sam-tagger
```

Python ≥ 3.13 is required. To run from source instead:

```bash
pixi install            # solves the env from pixi.toml
pixi run sam-tagger --version
```

# Prerequisite: the `cs` tag

Several features read the `cs` tag (produced by `minimap2 --cs`, or by a
cs-tagging step in your pipeline):

- **cs-dependent**: `--add-tc`, `--add-ee`, and the whole `error-stats`,
  `pileup`, and `qc-summary` (TC/error columns) commands.
- **cs-free**: `FL` and the CIGAR-derived tags `MS ME SS ES DM IL DL`.

If you enable a cs-dependent feature on a BAM whose reads lack `cs`, `sam-tagger`
prints an early warning (and a final summary) but continues — those tags/columns
will simply be empty.

# annotate

`annotate` is the only command that writes a BAM. It adds any subset of the
twelve tags, optionally extracts FASTQ, and optionally emits per-tag statistics
Parquet — all in a single pass.

```text
sam-tagger annotate INPUT-BAM OUTPUT-BAM [ARGS]
```

## Tags

The `--add-*` flags each take a **value: the BAM tag name to write**. By
convention the value matches the flag, but you can rename it if needed.

| Flag        | Value | Meaning                                              | Needs                |
|-------------|-------|------------------------------------------------------|----------------------|
| `--add-fl`  | `FL`  | `1` if the read spans the whole reference            | —                    |
| `--add-ms`  | `MS`  | Match start (1-based read position)                  | —                    |
| `--add-me`  | `ME`  | Match end (1-based read position)                    | —                    |
| `--add-tc`  | `TC`  | On-target (`OnTarget`) via cs, no errors in primers  | `--config`           |
| `--add-ap`  | `AP`  | Amplicon primer: `Both`/`StartOnly`/`EndOnly`/`Neither` | `--config`        |
| `--add-ss`  | `SS`  | Start (5′) soft-clip length                           | —                    |
| `--add-es`  | `ES`  | End (3′) soft-clip length                             | —                    |
| `--add-dm`  | `DM`  | Sum of M+D CIGAR ops (aligned ref length)            | —                    |
| `--add-ee`  | `EE`  | Error-event count from cs                            | cs                   |
| `--add-il`  | `IL`  | Longest insertion length in CIGAR                    | —                    |
| `--add-dl`  | `DL`  | Longest deletion length in CIGAR                     | —                    |
| `--add-nb`  | `NB`  | Next N reference bases after alignment end           | `--config` + `--fasta` |

The redundant legacy tags `HI`/`HD` (=IL>0/=DL>0) and `SP` (=SS+1) were removed.

## Extraction and statistics

| Flag                              | Takes      | Purpose                              |
|-----------------------------------|------------|--------------------------------------|
| `--extract-sub-reads-fastq`       | output path| Per-ref sub-reads to gzipped FASTQ   |
| `--extract-left-softclip-fastq`   | output path| 5′ soft-clips to gzipped FASTQ       |
| `--extract-right-softclip-fastq`  | output path| 3′ soft-clips to gzipped FASTQ       |
| `--fl-stats` / `--tc-stats` / `--ap-stats` / `--nb-stats` | output path | Per-tag statistics Parquet |

## Output format

`--output-format bam|cram|sam` (default `bam`). `cram` requires `--fasta` to
encode against. Input auto-detects BAM/CRAM/SAM. Use `-` for stdin/stdout.

## Examples

```bash
# CIGAR-only tags, no config needed
sam-tagger annotate aln.cs.bam out.bam --add-fl FL --add-ms MS --add-me ME

# Primer-dependent tags require a config
sam-tagger annotate aln.cs.bam out.bam \
    --config primers.csv \
    --add-fl FL --add-tc TC --add-ap AP --add-ee EE

# Write CRAM (--fasta mandatory), and add NB (also needs config + fasta)
sam-tagger annotate aln.cs.bam out.cram --output-format cram \
    --fasta ref.fa --config primers.csv \
    --add-fl FL --add-tc TC --add-ap AP --add-nb NB

# Tag the BAM and emit FL + AP statistics alongside
sam-tagger annotate aln.cs.bam out.bam \
    --config primers.csv \
    --add-fl FL --add-ap AP \
    --fl-stats fl.parquet --ap-stats ap.parquet

# Extract sub-reads (config supplies subread_start/subread_end)
sam-tagger annotate aln.cs.bam out.bam \
    --config primers.csv --add-fl FL \
    --extract-sub-reads-fastq subreads.fq.gz
```

# error-stats

```text
sam-tagger error-stats INPUT-BAM CONFIG [ARGS]
```

Read-only. Produces **seven** cs-tag error-statistics Parquet files. Give either
a `--prefix` (writes `{prefix}.error.parquet`, `{prefix}.mismatch.parquet`, …) or
the seven individual `--*-out` paths — the two are mutually exclusive.

| Output (`--prefix` writes `{p}.*`) | `--*-out` flag        | Contents                  |
|-----------------------------------|-----------------------|---------------------------|
| `{p}.error.parquet`               | `--error-out`         | Positional error counts   |

The `error` file splits each position's `mismatch` count by the read
(destination) base in `to_a`/`to_c`/`to_g`/`to_t`. A substitution whose read
base is N counts in `mismatch` only, so the four columns can sum below
`mismatch`.
| `{p}.mismatch.parquet`            | `--mismatch-out`      | Mismatch matrix           |
| `{p}.insertion.parquet`           | `--insertion-out`     | Insertion summary         |
| `{p}.deletion.parquet`            | `--deletion-out`      | Deletion summary          |
| `{p}.per_read.parquet`            | `--per-read-out`      | Per-read error            |
| `{p}.per_base.parquet`            | `--per-base-out`      | Per-base error            |
| `{p}.single_deletion.parquet`     | `--single-deletion-out` | Single-deletion counts  |

```bash
# prefix form (all 7 files at once)
sam-tagger error-stats aln.cs.bam primers.csv --prefix run1

# explicit-output form
sam-tagger error-stats aln.cs.bam primers.csv \
    --error-out err.parquet --mismatch-out mm.parquet \
    --insertion-out ins.parquet --deletion-out del.parquet \
    --per-read-out pr.parquet --per-base-out pb.parquet \
    --single-deletion-out sd.parquet
```

# pileup

```text
sam-tagger pileup INPUT-BAM OUTPUT [ARGS]
```

Read-only, bcftools-mpileup-like per-position statistics. Output columns:
`seq_name, pos, ref, alt, dp, adf, adr, ad, af`.

| Flag              | Purpose                                                  |
|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
| `--fasta`         | Indexed reference FASTA for `ref` bases (else `ref='.'`) |
| `--intervals`     | BED restricting which positions are reported             |
| `--min-base-qual` | Min base quality (Phred), default `20`                   |

```bash
sam-tagger pileup aln.cs.bam pileup.parquet --fasta ref.fa
sam-tagger pileup aln.cs.bam pileup.parquet --intervals targets.bed --min-base-qual 15
```

# qc-summary

```text
sam-tagger qc-summary INPUT-BAM OUTPUT [ARGS]
```

Read-only. One Parquet row per BAM-header reference, joining FL, TC, AP and
per-base error counts/rate into a single digest. Columns: `seq_name, total_reads,
fl, fl_pct, on_target, on_target_pct, ap_Both, ap_StartOnly, ap_EndOnly,
ap_Neither, mismatches, insertions, deletions, aligned_bases, error_rate`.
Zero-read references appear with zeros.

- **With `--config`** — all columns populate (TC/AP/error need primer params).
- **Without `--config`** — only `total_reads`, `fl`, `fl_pct` are computed.

```bash
# full summary
sam-tagger qc-summary aln.cs.bam qc.parquet --config primers.csv

# FL + read counts only (no primer config)
sam-tagger qc-summary aln.cs.bam qc.parquet
```

# Configuration (CSV)

Per-reference primer/sub-read/NB parameters live in one **wide CSV** file (one
row per reference), validated by pydantic. `seq_name` must match a `@SQ SN` in
the BAM header (because `seq_name`/`seq_len` come from the header — `seq_len` is
not in the CSV). Empty cells mean "unset"; unknown columns, duplicate/empty
`seq_name`, and wrong-typed values are hard errors.

```csv
seq_name,tc_primer_start_len,tc_primer_end_len,amp_primer_start_len,amp_primer_end_len,amp_primer_start_seq,amp_primer_end_seq,error_primer_start_len,error_primer_end_len,subread_start,subread_end,next_n
seq1,8,8,9,7,GGGGGGGGG,CCCCCCC,5,5,12,21,6
150-1-P,,,,,,,,10,10,,
```

A complete example ships at [`config.example.csv`](../config.example.csv).

| Config column                                            | Drives                                    |
|----------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `tc_primer_start_len` / `tc_primer_end_len`              | `--add-tc`, `--tc-stats`                  |
| `amp_primer_*_len`, `amp_primer_*_seq`                   | `--add-ap`, `--ap-stats`                  |
| `error_primer_start_len` / `error_primer_end_len`        | `error-stats`                             |
| `subread_start` / `subread_end`                          | `--extract-sub-reads-fastq`               |
| `next_n`                                                 | `--add-nb`, `--nb-stats` (needs `--fasta`) |

`FL` and the CIGAR-only tags need **no** config.

# Python API

Every subcommand is also callable in-process. The four orchestrators, their args
dataclasses, the collectors, and `load_config` are re-exported via `__all__`:

```python
from pathlib import Path
from sam_tagger import AnnotateArgs, run_annotate, load_config

run_annotate(AnnotateArgs(
    input_bam=Path("aln.cs.bam"),
    output_bam=Path("out.bam"),
    add_fl="FL",
    add_tc="TC",
    config=Path("primers.csv"),
))
```

The args dataclass is the single source of truth — the same `AnnotateArgs` /
`ErrorStatsArgs` / `PileupArgs` / `QcSummaryArgs` back both the CLI flags and the
Python call, so nothing drifts between the two surfaces.

# Help and verbosity

```bash
sam-tagger --help                 # list subcommands
sam-tagger annotate --help        # full flag reference for one command
sam-tagger -v annotate in.bam out.bam --add-fl FL   # -v INFO, -vv DEBUG, -vvv TRACE
```
